q-161133.name: Question 1
q-161133.problem:
$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

Consider the surface integral of the function 
$f(x,y,z)=x+z$ 
over the parametric surface 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨uv,\,{u}^{2},\,{v}^{2}⟩
$$

for $(u,v)\in D⊆{R}^{2}.$ What is the missing expression?

*Hint: You can use the fact that $‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=\sqrt{16{u}^{2}{v}^{2}+4{v}^{4}+4{u}^{4}}.$*
q-161133.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

Notice that we are told that the norm of the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=\sqrt{16{u}^{2}{v}^{2}+4{v}^{4}+4{u}^{4}}.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(x+z)\,{|}_{x=uv\,y={u}^{2}\,z={v}^{2}} \\  & =uv+{v}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,(uv+{v}^{2})\sqrt{16{u}^{2}{v}^{2}+4{v}^{4}+4{u}^{4}}\,\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

q-161288.name: Question 2
q-161288.problem:
$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

Consider the surface integral of the function 
$f(x,y,z)=-x-{z}^{2}$ 
over the parametric surface 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨{u}^{3},\,v,\,{v}^{2}⟩
$$

for $(u,v)\in D⊆{R}^{2}.$ What is the missing expression?
q-161288.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{3}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨3{u}^{2},\,0,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{3}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,2v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 3{u}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2v\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2v\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}3{u}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 2v\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}3{u}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-6v{u}^{2},\,3{u}^{2}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨0,\,-6v{u}^{2},\,3{u}^{2}⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(0)^{2}+(-6v{u}^{2})^{2}+(3{u}^{2})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36{v}^{2}{u}^{4}+9{u}^{4}} \\  & =3{u}^{2}\sqrt{4{v}^{2}+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(-x-{z}^{2})\,{|}_{x={u}^{3}\,y=v\,z={v}^{2}} \\  & =-{u}^{3}-({v}^{2}\cdot {v}^{2}) \\  & =-{u}^{3}-{v}^{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as 

$$

q-161135.name: Question 3
q-161135.problem:
$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

Consider the surface integral of the function 
$f(x,y,z)=xz+y$ 
over the parametric surface 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,-v,\,-{v}^{2}⟩
$$

for $(u,v)\in D⊆{R}^{2}.$ What is the missing expression?

*Hint: You can use the fact that $‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=\sqrt{1+4{v}^{2}}.$*
q-161135.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

Notice that we are told that the norm of the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=\sqrt{1+4{v}^{2}}.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(xz+y)\,{|}_{x=u\,y=-v\,z={v}^{2}} \\  & =u\cdot (-{v}^{2})+(-v) \\  & =-u{v}^{2}-v\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,(-u{v}^{2}-v)\sqrt{1+4{v}^{2}}\,\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}

q-161124.problem:

$$

Consider the surface integral of the function 
$f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}$ 
over the parametric surface 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,u,\,v⟩
$$

for $(u,v)\in D⊆{R}^{2}.$ What is the missing expression?
q-161124.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,0⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨1,\,-1,\,0⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(0)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+1+0} \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,{|}_{x=u\,y=u\,z=v} \\  & ={u}^{2}+{u}^{2} \\  & =2{u}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,2\sqrt{2}{u}^{2}\,\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

q-160712.problem:
$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

Consider the surface integral of the function 
$f(x,y,z)=x+y+z$ 
over the parametric surface 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨{u}^{2},\,u-{v}^{2},\,{v}^{2}⟩
$$

for $(u,v)\in D⊆{R}^{2}.$ What is the missing expression?

*Hint: You can use the fact that $‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=2v\sqrt{1+8{u}^{2}}.$*
q-160712.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

Notice that we are told that the norm of the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=\sqrt{{u}^{2}+{v}^{2}+1}.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(x+y+z)\,{|}_{x={u}^{2}\,y=u-{v}^{2}\,z={v}^{2}} \\  & ={u}^{2}+(u-{v}^{2})+{v}^{2} \\  & ={u}^{2}+u\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,2({u}^{2}+u)v\sqrt{1+8{u}^{2}}\,\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

q-160834.name: Question 6
q-160834.problem:
Evaluate the surface integral 

$$
{∬}_{S}(2x+y+z)\,\text{d}S,
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨2u-v,\,3u+2,\,u+2v⟩
$$

 
over the domain $D={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,-1\le v\le 1}.$

*Hint: You can use the fact that $‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=\sqrt{70}.$*
q-160834.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

Notice that we are told that the norm of the fundamental vector product is

$$
‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=\sqrt{70}.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(2x+y+z)\,{|}_{x=2u-v\,y=3u+2\,z=u+2v} \\  & =2(2u-v)+(3u+2)+(u+2v) \\  & =8u+2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,(8u+2)\sqrt{70}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{70}{∬}_{D}\,(8u+2)\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{70}{\int }_{0}^{1}(8u+2)\,\text{d}u\cdot {\int }_{-1}^{1}\,\text{d}v \\  & =\sqrt{70}\cdot [4{u}^{2}+2u]_{0}^{1}\cdot [u]_{-1}^{1} \\  & =\sqrt{70}\cdot 6\cdot 2 \\  & =12\sqrt{70}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(3x-2y+3z)\,{|}_{x=2u+v\,y=2u+v\,z=-v} \\  & =3(2u+v)-2(2u+v)+3(-v) \\  & =2(u-v)\end{aligned}

q-160835.name: Question 9
q-160835.problem:
Evaluate the surface integral 

$$
{∬}_{S}4xy\,\text{d}S,
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by the equations

$$
x=u,\,y=v,\,z=6-3u-2v
$$

for $0\le u\le 2$ and $0\le v\le 3.$
q-160835.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,6-3u-2v⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(6-3u-2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-3⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(6-3u-2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨3,\,2,\,1⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨3,\,2,\,1⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9+4+1} \\  & =\sqrt{14}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =4xy\,{|}_{x=u\,y=v\,z=6-3u-2v} \\  & =4uv\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if we denote 

$$
D={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 2,\,0\le v\le 3},
$$

our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}4xy\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,4uv\sqrt{14}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{14}{∬}_{D}\,4uv\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{14}{\int }_{0}^{2}2u\,\text{d}u\cdot {\int }_{0}^{3}2v\,\text{d}v \\  & =\sqrt{14}\cdot [{u}^{2}]_{0}^{2}\cdot [{v}^{2}]_{0}^{3} \\  & =\sqrt{14}\cdot 4\cdot 9 \\  & =36\sqrt{14}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-161179.name: Question 10
q-161179.problem:
Evaluate the surface integral 

$$
{∬}_{S}(x+y+z)\,\text{d}S,
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u+v,\,3v,\,2u-v⟩
$$

 
over the domain $D={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 1}.$

*Hint: You can use the fact that $‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=3\sqrt{6}.$*
q-161179.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

Notice that we are told that the norm of the fundamental vector product is

$$
‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=3\sqrt{6}.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(x+y+z)\,{|}_{x=u+v\,y=3v\,z=2u-v} \\  & =(u+v)+(3v)+(2u-v) \\  & =3u+3v\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,(3u+3v)\cdot 3\sqrt{6}\,\text{d}A \\  & =9\sqrt{6}{∬}_{D}\,(u+v)\,\text{d}A \\  & =9\sqrt{6}{\int }_{0}^{1}({\int }_{0}^{1}u+v\,\text{d}u)\text{d}v \\  & =9\sqrt{6}{\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{{u}^{2}}{2}+vu]}_{0}^{1}\text{d}v \\  & =9\sqrt{6}{\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{1}{2}+v)\text{d}v \\  & =9\sqrt{6}{[\frac{v}{2}+\frac{{v}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =9\sqrt{6}\cdot 1 \\  & =9\sqrt{6}.\end{aligned}
$$
